posts.title: [MOC] 42145 B Model - Flight Control Set
posts.text: Since 42145 is all about aircraft controls, it is only fitting that its alternate model should revolve around the same concept. Combine that with my penchant for mini models, and voila! MINI AIRCRAFTS I chose to do 3 different types of aircrafts to increase playability. The seaplane is intended to be a mini 42040, as a homage to the first aircraft set I bought after returning to Lego (2015) and also the set that taught me about flight controls. The jet is based on the 42040 B Model, with the twin tails taken from 42066 Air Race Jet, and the function taken from 42044. Since there is only one pair of small wheels, the front wheel of the jet has to use the Bionicle ball instead. The helicopter is just a generic design that reuses the 3x3 disc as a fenestron. All three of them have connection interfaces that allow them to fit on the bars on the control set. CONTROL SET The control set use the same principles in the main model and is based on the layout of a plane's cockpit. There are three levers that control three different movements of an airplane. The joystick allows the plane to roll and pitch. The two pedals allow the plane to yaw. The side lever is intended to be the collective pitch control, which lifts the whole aircraft through changing the angle of attack. DEMONSTRATION INSTRUCTION https://reb.li/m/281305

posts.title: Prototyping Pins Using Dowels
posts.text: I got some of my 3rd party brand pins sanded down , but its slow so I need to find a better method These are for prototyping models, they make it easier to modify stuff because they can be pushed or pulled out since they don't have the stop rings however I'm also designing a standard for building that tries to ensure they can be pulled or pushed out by prioritizing pinholes or empty space on at least one side of the pin 2L axle pins 99% of the time, won't need prototyping variants, because pins cannot go thru axle holes anyway It should be easy enough to take an assembly apart enough using these brown/green prototyping pins to remove axle pins anyway But if needs must then I guess a 2L bar + stud-pin is almost like a 2L axle pin And if the stud is in the way then either a 1L pneumatic hose with a 2L rigid hose inserted 2L pin with 1L axle (11214) can be replicated with 2 parts , a bar 2L and a friction less 2L pin or the brown 2L prototyping pin - frictionless prevents the bar going too far in that's all For a 2L axle with 1L pin (18651/65249) we're back to using stud-pins and 3L bars assuming you're using this in a pinhole - axle-hole - axle-hole rather than a pinhole - pinhole -axle hole If not than you just use a 2Lpin with 1L axle part (11214), or the substitution I mentioned

posts.title: Wizarding World 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: Yeah, if the Azkaban rumour is legit then it makes the most sense to see it in the vein of other "dark" locations like Grimmauld Place, the Ministry (the original playset), Malfoy Manor, and maythe the Lovegood House. Which gives us a range of EUR 100-150, and the knowledge that the bigger the building, the more it will resemble a flat facade. Azkaban unlike Malfoy Manor is just narrow and tall (similar to the Lovegood House) so it would hopefully be less facade-like. They also tend to "childify" those dark locations by either including "humourous" scenes (like with the Weasleys at Grimmauld Place) or making up bizarre interiors (i.e. the throne-like loo at Malfoy Manor, and Narcissa wrestling a giant lobster in the kitchen, while there's no inclusion of the canonical prisoner dungeons). They're even doing the latter across other themes (Barad-Dur over at LotR has an Orc cafeteria, and the Death Star over at SW has a hot tub for Stormtroopers). So I'd expect something in that vein.

posts.title: [MOC] Danish Rubber Noses - An Ongoing Saga
posts.text: Thank you for all your nice comments! 😭 Yes! Even 36 years after entering service, the IC3 DMU (And partly the IR4 EMU) is still the backbone of Danish long distance train services. They were supposed to retire now, but with another delay of the IC5 which was supposed to enter service this year, the IC3's will probably still be around for a while. I'm probably biased, as this is a train I've seen all my life, but I love the design! I don't see it as ugly at all! This is the train that pops into my head when I think of a passenger train in general. Every Dane probably thinks this, and either knows it by the name "IC3" or simply just as a "DSB train". Thank you! The rubber nose is definitely the part of the train that I am the most proud of 😊 Joining BSBT 2026 was an awesome experience! We all got to meet so many of the great builders whose models we already knew from forums like this and Flickr. it was a lot of fun driving around between so many other nationalities, and seeing the visitors recognizing the train and taking photos/videos. Haha, that would be the next step! Though, probably not possible to do "legally" with the parts selection available at the moment. I saw someone who did an IC3 MOC where they used technic tube for the rubber front, probably to mimic the air-filled rubber hose, but I don't think it looked that nice... (Probably not helped by the fact that this build is from 2007 or earlier) By heino at Brickshelf.com And ending off with another shot of my IC3 train and IR4 train coupled together, just because :)) More photos on my Flickr account

posts.title: Wizarding World 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: Y’know, when I said we should start getting leaks on the summer wave soon yesterday, I wasn’t expecting this soon. Another leak reporting the Astronomy Tower (and seemingly confirming we will have two castle systems going at once) is exciting. GoF wouldn’t have been my choice for that section, but given the very limited in castle options for that movie, it looks like we’ll be seeing the prefects’ bath and trophy room at the very least, and I do think those will turn out well in this system. Azkaban is a little baffling though. Sure, it’s one of the few places that haven’t been done in Harry Potter Lego, but that’s because to do the triangular monolith building shown in OotP at a scale even close to being compatible for minifigures would require a pretty steep price – and between the dark subject matter, lack of main characters, ridiculously short time on screen, and at least half the included minifigs being dementor repeats, I’m just not sure how many people would be willing to pay for that. What I could see Lego doing is testing the waters on how popular Azkaban is by doing it as a second installment of sorts in the mini buildings line after the $40 Hogwarts we got this year. I doubt we’ll see Myrtle in the prefects’ bathroom. Yes, she appears in the scene – but Nick was an iconic part of the first Great Hall scene and didn’t show up there in anticipation for pairing him with the Gryffindor common room the next year, and Quirrel is kinda the whole point of the trio facing the forbidden corridor challenges and he doesn’t show up in the Grand Staircase Tower because he’d already shown up in the Great Hall. The designers just don’t seem to want to repeat minor characters in the large castle sets for this system. I also wouldn’t expect another Yule Ball castle section. The ball happens in the Great Hall and simply doesn’t fit anywhere else. Lego only got away with putting it with another section of the castle back in 2019 by having everything about the ball be a side build completely separate from the set’s actual castle.

posts.title: Using Claude AI for new ports and translations
posts.text: Patience, Evan, patience—no need to use all capital letters. I am "almost" there; currently my 4.5V/12V trains from 1973(!) onwards are remotely controlled via LEGO Blockly. Their original motors, that is - using "slightly modified" PF receivers. As you know, LEGO Blockly can not only do PF IR (and now even 433 MHz RF PF, as per my “suggestion” to Yves), but also readily control multiple Int.A and Int.B. And almost all the "rest" of LEGO interfaces/PBricks. I am currently trying to figure out what to do with my Int.A's. There are soo many options. Stocked up 4.5V motors and cables; I just need additional sensors. Although, as I am not a purist, I really want to exploit Int.A's absolutely stunning handling of signal changes (on different DC biases—it does not care about DC; it sees changes). All work in mental progress. It is ashamed that TLG never introduced further sensors for Int.A Have a very nice weekend + all the best Thorsten

posts.title: Lego Blockly: Graphical Common Programming Environment Web App (Using Intuitive Blockly) for All Lego Robotic Platforms.
posts.text: And THAT IS FUN to do! It is so nice to see my 4.5V steam train, which was released in 1972, steaming on when pulling a LEGO Blockly slider up! A 2026 programming environment acting as a client to a powerful modern microcontroller, which sends out, with the help of a 15-year-old LINX 433 Mhz transmitter and receiver, data to a pimped PF receiver from 2010 (the code says), which in turn turns on a 4.5V train motor - with PF PWM. I'd say this is playing across multiple themes and generations of technology. I simply love that. Best Thorsten

posts.text: Mine arrived two days ago. No notification apart from DPD: "Your package arrives soon." That was 4 days ago. It said "from LEGO/Denmark". Cryptic numbers on the box, but it said "from LEGO/Denmark". I opened it - and then BOOOOM it all came back. I am getting older - but apparently had negotiated favorably with headquarters here back in summer. It was like in Total Recall: This was intended to be a 2026 Christmas gift for whoever in the family wanted to spend €120 (or less, as I suggested that maybe I can chip in as well) ... and then the purchase was cleared. Only one unit due to severe LEGO budget limitation ("one day, your entire attic will be crashing down onto the 2nd floor") along with severe attic space limitations (same argument applies; she may be right after all ...). Now comes the best part: Headquarters doesn't recall that deal!!! You know what this means? My Christmas wishlist is >totally< empty! posts.text: That is so true! However, the MPLab X IDE or the VSCode plugin from microchip is still good for programming and flashing the smallest PICs, e.g. my beloved PIC12F508 - and they still sell it! Back to the 433 MHz technology of more than two decades ago! OK, I used a "modern" version of the LINX TXM433 module, the TXM-LR series. LINX is not LINX anymore, as it has been acquired by TE Connectivity (I believe it was around 2022), but they still develop RF modules! And all major distributors (Farnell etc.) still have the good old TXM and RXM modules for sale. So, I am totally UP-TO-DATE!!! Here is the thing: I have 8 LEGO trains running on RF-PF, as my layout is mostly behind stuff, where IR never gets :D. There are: #181 4.5V Steam Train (PF receivers run fine on 4.5V!), #727 12V Diesel Locomotive, #7740 12V Intercity Train (PF receivers also run fine on 12V), and then 5 more "modern" 9V trains like #4512 (PF receivers also run fine on 9V), and PF retrofitted trains like the #12219 Maersk cargo train. They all have RF receivers plugged in and I simply don't want to change that to BLE or the like ;) Even better: IT ALL WORKS!!! My trains respond nicely (as per today) to LEGO Blockly using PF blocks. Here is the little 433MHz extension for the LEGO Blockly ESP32 PFIR server (range is about 10 m, more than enough in my attic ;) @Bliss: The flashing (version V8) is absolutely comfortable! Thank you so much for all you have done (for me, as I believe there are no further 433MHz LEGO PF users :) All the best, Thorsten

posts.title: DC Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: That's good, but I still think Peter Jackson in a Prancing Pony set is a vastly more understandable decision than if Gunn is the missing Daily Planet minifigure. (Also, we should get a Tolkien. I'm not saying Peter Jackson doesn't also deserve it, but we should get Tolkien) As for Harry Potter, sure some people would probably complain nowadays if they did JK Rowling, but my point is moreso the theme is in a much better state than DC- I think almost every non-extra is covered at this point- and yet they haven't had a Chris Columbus minifigure or anything (who I'd consider about as crucial to Harry Potter's movie success as Jackson was to LOTR- not that they're the same type of movie). It would just be ridiculous if a theme that had two characters this year would expend one of it's rare figure slots on a guy who's made one moderately successful film for the franchise. It would make sense if we were missing Perry/Lombardi/Grant or something- easy to add a few kitbashes. "Me and chip, we stood right here, chip and I" -Guy when Clark asks why none of the other Green Lanterns showed up to his set release. Absolutely. Though you never know, the missing character could always be a blue and red batsuit or something. I wouldn't call it cowardly- objectively speaking a set like this in the current state of the theme is a huge swing. It seems objectively smart to keep it comic based so if MoT doesn't do too well, it won't automatically sink the set. If they were being cowardly, this would be another batman set. I don't know how likely it is that there's a full third of the figure list missing, but I do like these three comparisons.

posts.title: DC Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: Here’s my expectations and what I’d really like to see for all the figures: Superman: I expect it’ll be a reuse of the 2025 one with new legs. I’d love to see dual molded boots with printing for the trunks, but I’d settle even for how they handled Wolverine in the X-Jet. I’d also love to see his original hairpiece with the curl make a comeback. Clark Kent: probably a kitbash with maybe a new face print Lois Lane: probably a kitbash Jimmy Olsen: definitely a kitbash, my only hope is they don’t give him the Professor Xavier head Supergirl: probably going to be the red skirt version, although I’d love to see the white shirt version or the blue skirt version just to give some variety from the last version Mr Terrific: Really hoping he has printed legs and I think there’s a good shot it happens Guy Gardener: Really hoping he doesn’t have the Bruce Wayne head. It’s also be great to see the green lantern mold return from the CMF Hawkgirl: pretty sure this is gonna be Kendra and I’m fine with that since we already got Shayera. Mostly I just want a new helmet mold for her. The Hawkman helmet did not work for the last Hawkgirl. Metamorpho: I already have the CMF figure and I don’t see this one improving on that. But it is still nice to see him. Krypto: not sure how they can improve on the previous one, so I’d be fine with that one coming back. A new mold would be cool too. Lex Luthor: probably going to be the 2025 version and I’m happy with that. But I’d love to get a different head for him. Brainiac: probably going to be the New 52 design and I’m cool with that. Would love to see him get some printed legs and a more appropriate expression (namely, expressionless) for the head print. Mystery character(s): Perry White, Cat Grant, Ron Troupe, and Steve Lombard would all be great additions even if they would just be kitbash. Bizarro, Zod, and Doomsday would also be welcome additions, but I don’t see them happening. Maybe if the set sells well we can get a Fortress of Solitude down the line with one of them.
